title: Feasibility and pilot study of an outpatient music therapy concept for patients with depressive symptoms
summary:
Background: Outpatient treatment with music therapy is not yet part of the prescription of remedies for patients with depressive symptoms in Germany and can only be obtained by patients at their own expense. At the same time, depression and depressive symptoms are among the most common mental illnesses in Germany. Due long waiting times for conselling, a resource-oriented, short term music therapy intervention in the form of outpatient group music therapy could stabilise patients with depressive symptoms during the waiting period and optimise therapeutic outpatient care overall.

Research questions: From the perspective of patients and experts, what aspects need to be considered in short-term group music therapy interventions for the outpatient treatment of patients with depressive symptoms? What factors influence the recruitment of patients with depressive symptoms from general practices? How do patients with depressive symptoms rate the short-term group music therapy intervention?

Methods: In study part A, the outpatient concept for the treamtnet of patients with depressive symptoms is developed. Appyling a nominal group process, people with lived experience in depressive symptoms as well as experts from music therapy research and practice meet online. A separate approach will be developed in each group at first, and combined to the final concept in the end.
In study part B, the feasibility of the concept is tested and piloted. Patients are recruited from general practitioners' practices. In six groups of six participants each, the participants receive the short-term music therapy intervention in one of the study centers (Hamburg or Heidelberg). Before the start and after the end of the short-term intervention, a telephone survey is conducted using a standardised questionnaire. In addition, participants are asked to provide a subjective appraisal rating after each session.

interventions.name:
Patients with depressive symptoms receive short-term outpatient music therapy in a group of six people over six sessions of 100 minutes each.
